title: Retail Credit Risk

maps.tested: The sheet narrows Reading 25 to two LOs and tells you to give the rating-agency methodologies a careful read rather than memorise them.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'retail credit'. The examinable retail-specific material is the risk-based-pricing / adverse-selection dynamic and the dark-side-of-retail-credit argument. Rating agency methodologies (Reading 24) sit alongside as a read-only item.

vardeezReading: CR-7: Moderate, "LO 25.f: & LO 25.h: can be important here"; CR-6: Moderate, "Credit rating agency methodologies (just give a good read for this)".

selectors.name: Risk-based pricing and adverse selection
selectors.what: Under a one price fits all policy in a competitive market the bank attracts mainly high-risk customers and repels low-risk ones, and the damage may only show in a downturn; risk-based (tiered) pricing sets the price by score, so a higher score band gets a lower price.

selectors.name: The dark side of retail credit
selectors.what: The danger that losses suddenly rise to unexpected levels because of an unforeseen systematic risk factor that affects many small credits at once (new products, a perfect storm of risk factors, changed attitudes to default, operational issues), and the measures against it: limited exposure to new risks and stress testing. A single large name loss is the corporate profile, not this.

selectors.name: Retail versus corporate credit risk
selectors.what: Retail portfolios of many small, homogeneous loans behave like diversified portfolios, so expected loss is predictable and priced as a cost of doing business, and regulatory capital is small but not zero; corporate portfolios carry large single-name exposures and concentrations, and their risk is dominated by unexpected loss.

selectors.name: CAP and accuracy ratio
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'CAP and accuracy ratio' on CR-7 f
selectors.what: Scorecard performance: the cumulative accuracy profile plots cumulative actual defaults against the population sorted from highest to lowest risk score, the perfect model captures all defaults in the first default-rate slice and the random model is the 45-degree line; the accuracy ratio is the area under the actual model over the area under the perfect model, both measured against the random line, and closer to 1 is better.
